headline: Preliminary count at 21.5% of voting places: National 30.0%, Labour 29.4%
body: Updated preliminary party-vote figures carried by RNZ, using Electoral Commission data, put National on 30.0% and Labour on 29.4%, with the Greens on 13.5%, ACT on 10.8%, NZ First on 9.6%, Opportunity on 5.4% and Te Pāti Māori on 0.5%. RNZ’s seat table, supplied by the Commission, shows National on 42 seats, Labour 35, Greens 16, ACT 13, NZ First 12, Opportunity 7 and Te Pāti Māori 5, for a 130-seat Parliament with overhang. These figures cover the 21.5% of voting places that had reported, not 21.5% of votes. Electorate seats in that table are current leads, not confirmed wins. Preliminary results leave out special votes and will change as counting continues. Official results are expected on 27 November.

headline: First preliminary party vote: National ahead with 8.2% of voting places reported
body: Early preliminary figures carried by RNZ, using Electoral Commission data, show National on 31.2% of the party vote and Labour on 28.4%, followed by the Greens (12.8%), ACT (11.2%), NZ First (9.7%) and Opportunity (5.7%). These figures cover only the 8.2% of voting places that had reported, not 8.2% of votes. Preliminary results leave out special votes and will change as counting goes on. Official results are expected on 27 November.
